{ "source": "{% extends 'OT Layout' %} {% block content %} {% comment %} Case worklist and search (PP-04). Filtering and paging both happen server-side in FetchXML. Nothing is filtered in the browser and no unbounded set is retrieved (NFR-PERF-01). Filter values are escaped before they reach the query. Option-set values come from src/Entities/al_OutcomeCase/Entity.xml: al_casestatus 120910580-120910592, al_priority 120910780-120910783, al_casetype 120910510-120910513. These are schema values, not display strings, so referencing them directly is safe. Two scopes share this page. `?mine=1` is the reviewer's own worklist - the cases carrying a review instance assigned to the signed-in contact (AD-047, AD-050) - and the bare URL is every case. My Work's "My cases" tile and the primary-navigation "Cases" link used to point at the same unscoped URL, so a tile that counted nine opened a list of thirteen; the tile now carries the parameter and this page honours it. Scoping is presentation, never a boundary. Under OD-022 every authenticated user may read every case, and the write boundary is the Contact-anchored table permission chain (AD-056, AD-069). What the scope buys is a reviewer seeing their own work first. {% endcomment %} {% assign f_ref = request.params['ref'] | default: '' %} {% assign f_client = request.params['client'] | default: '' %} {% assign f_adviser = request.params['adviser'] | default: '' %} {% assign f_status = request.params['status'] | default: '' %} {% assign f_priority = request.params['priority'] | default: '' %} {% assign f_type = request.params['type'] | default: '' %} {% assign f_from = request.params['from'] | default: '' %} {% assign f_to = request.params['to'] | default: '' %} {% assign f_outcome = request.params['outcome'] | default: '' %} {% comment %} `mine` is a scope, not a filter: it does not appear in the filter chips or count towards has_filter, because "my cases, unfiltered" is a starting point rather than a search the user should be invited to clear. It is dropped for an anonymous visitor - an unguarded {{ user.id }} would emit an empty condition value and match every row, turning "my cases" into "all cases" silently, which is the exact over-report this parameter exists to stop. {% endcomment %} {% assign f_mine = request.params['mine'] | default: '' %} {% if user == null %}{% assign f_mine = '' %}{% endif %} {% if f_mine != '' and f_mine != '1' %}{% assign f_mine = '' %}{% endif %} {% comment %} Outcome filter (PP-17). This is the list the outcome cards on Home drill into, so the parameter is a slug rather than an option-set number: a shared link reads as /cases?outcome=harm, and no Dataverse internal is exposed in a URL a person can see. A case's grade lives on al_outcome, not on the case, and BR-007 splits it across two columns so a regrade preserves both. "Effective grade is X" therefore means final = X, OR final is empty AND initial = X - which is why each slug carries the pair of option values and the filter below is an OR containing a nested AND. The values are the two option sets in src/Entities/al_Outcome/Entity.xml. An unrecognised slug is cleared rather than ignored. Ignoring it would drop the condition and show every case under a "Filtered cases" heading - a wrong answer that looks like a right one. {% endcomment %} {% assign o_final = '' %} {% assign o_initial = '' %} {% case f_outcome %} {% when 'pass' %}{% assign o_final = '120910710' %}{% assign o_initial = '120910700' %} {% when 'issues' %}{% assign o_final = '120910711' %}{% assign o_initial = '120910701' %} {% when 'insufficient' %}{% assign o_final = '120910712' %}{% assign o_initial = '120910702' %} {% when 'harm' %}{% assign o_final = '120910713' %}{% assign o_initial = '120910703' %} {% endcase %} {% if f_outcome != '' and f_outcome != 'none' and o_final == '' %}{% assign f_outcome = '' %}{% endif %} {% comment %} Review route filter (project owner, 2026-09-10). Read from the environment rather than listed here: al_reviewroute's ids are the environment's own, so hard-coding them would break anywhere but DEV - the same reason DeriveRoute looks a route up by its code. Validated against the ids just fetched, which is this page's rule for every parameter that reaches FetchXML: an unrecognised value becomes no filter rather than a condition. {% endcomment %} {% fetchxml routes %} {% endfetchxml %} {% assign f_route = request.params['route'] | default: '' %} {% assign route_ok = false %} {% if f_route != '' %} {% for r in routes.results.entities %} {% if r.al_reviewrouteid == f_route %}{% assign route_ok = true %}{% endif %} {% endfor %} {% endif %} {% unless route_ok %}{% assign f_route = '' %}{% endunless %} {% assign has_filter = false %} {% if f_ref != '' or f_client != '' or f_adviser != '' or f_status != '' or f_priority != '' or f_type != '' or f_from != '' or f_to != '' or f_outcome != '' or f_route != '' %}{% assign has_filter = true %}{% endif %} {% comment %} `integer` is the only safe coercion here. `times: 1` repeats a string rather than converting it, so page_number became a string collection and the comparison below threw. `default` cannot rescue that - it only substitutes null. {% endcomment %} {% assign page_size = 25 %} {% assign page_number = request.params['page'] | integer | default: 1 %} {% if page_number < 1 %}{% assign page_number = 1 %}{% endif %} {% capture qs %}mine={{ f_mine | url_escape }}&ref={{ f_ref | url_escape }}&client={{ f_client | url_escape }}&adviser={{ f_adviser | url_escape }}&status={{ f_status | url_escape }}&priority={{ f_priority | url_escape }}&type={{ f_type | url_escape }}&from={{ f_from | url_escape }}&to={{ f_to | url_escape }}&outcome={{ f_outcome | url_escape }}&route={{ f_route | url_escape }}{% endcapture %} {% comment %} Case dashboard (PP-04). Five stages and a total, each one a card that opens the very list it counted. The point of a number on a dashboard is that you can act on it, so every card links to a filter this page already supports rather than to a view that has to be assembled by hand; a card whose drill-down did not exist would be decoration. The stages are the ones where a case is WAITING FOR SOMEONE - queued for a checker, assigned and not started, being checked, submitted, awaiting the adviser. Closed and No check required are deliberately absent: they are not work, and putting them on a dashboard invites reading the biggest number as the most important one. Imported, Validation failed and Ready for allocation belong to intake, which happens in the app, not here. Each card honours the scope. Under "My cases" the counts and the links both carry mine=1, so the figure on a card and the count on the page it opens are the same number - the mismatch AD-047 already had to fix once between My Work's tile and this list. Six small aggregates rather than one grouped query, for the reason the Home cards record: a grouped fetch would make the page depend on how an aliased choice column renders in Liquid, and a card showing "120910583" instead of a stage is worse than a sixth round trip. Status values are numeric literals from src/Entities/al_OutcomeCase/Entity.xml. {% endcomment %} {% capture scope_qs %}{% if f_mine == '1' %}mine=1&{% endif %}{% endcapture %} {% fetchxml n_queued %} {% if f_mine == '1' %}{% endif %} {% endfetchxml %} {% fetchxml n_assigned %} {% if f_mine == '1' %}{% endif %} {% endfetchxml %} {% fetchxml n_inprogress %} {% if f_mine == '1' %}{% endif %} {% endfetchxml %} {% fetchxml n_submitted %} {% if f_mine == '1' %}{% endif %} {% endfetchxml %} {% fetchxml n_remediation %} {% if f_mine == '1' %}{% endif %} {% endfetchxml %} {% comment %} An aggregate fetch returns no result set at all when the caller cannot read the table, and indexing entities[0] straight away then fails with "Index was outside the bounds of the array" - which renders as the card's number. Same guard as Home and My Work, for the same reason: a card shows a figure or nothing, never an error string. {% endcomment %} {% assign c_queued = 0 %}{% if n_queued.results and n_queued.results.entities.size > 0 %}{% assign c_queued = n_queued.results.entities[0].total %}{% endif %} {% assign c_assigned = 0 %}{% if n_assigned.results and n_assigned.results.entities.size > 0 %}{% assign c_assigned = n_assigned.results.entities[0].total %}{% endif %} {% assign c_inprogress = 0 %}{% if n_inprogress.results and n_inprogress.results.entities.size > 0 %}{% assign c_inprogress = n_inprogress.results.entities[0].total %}{% endif %} {% assign c_submitted = 0 %}{% if n_submitted.results and n_submitted.results.entities.size > 0 %}{% assign c_submitted = n_submitted.results.entities[0].total %}{% endif %} {% assign c_remediation = 0 %}{% if n_remediation.results and n_remediation.results.entities.size > 0 %}{% assign c_remediation = n_remediation.results.entities[0].total %}{% endif %} {% comment %} The stage tiles, drawn as My work draws its own: the strip opens the page rather than sitting inside a card. It used to be wrapped in one, with a header bar and an intro paragraph, so the same component read as a bordered box inside a bordered box and did not match the page it was copied from (project owner, 2026-09-13: "ensure that the cards styling on cases match that of the my work page"). The heading went with the wrapper, and with it a count of every case. Neither is missed: the card immediately below names the same scope - My cases, All cases, Filtered cases - and carries its own total, and each tile still says what it counts. A bare

was not an option in its place; nothing in the stylesheet dresses one outside a card, so it would have arrived as a browser default, which is the fault this change exists to remove. {% endcomment %}

Inner, because a case with no review assigned to this contact is not their case. Joined on the review rather than on al_caseassignment so the list matches the "Reviews assigned to you" table on My Work, which reads the same lookup - a case can be allocated and its review reassigned, and it is the review that says whose work it is now. A case carrying both a Tax and an AQS review assigned to the same person matches this join twice, which is why the fetch above turns on distinct when the scope is active. Without it a reviewer holding both disciplines on one case would see it listed twice and the page count would disagree with the tile. {% endcomment %} {% if f_mine == '1' %}{% endif %} {% comment %} Outer, and joined on the case rather than the review: a case with no outcome yet must still appear in an unfiltered list, and "Not yet graded" is a real drill-down target from the Home cards. An inner join would silently drop every ungraded case from the whole worklist. One row per case, not several. al_outcome is written only by the AQS branch of SubmitReviewPlugin, on a review instance whose code ClaimCasePlugin makes deterministic per case and discipline; a regrade updates al_finaloutcome on that same row (BR-007) rather than adding another. So this join cannot multiply a case across pages, and the grade below is unambiguous. {% endcomment %} {% comment %} Outer, for the reason the outcome join above is: a case is routed by DeriveRoute from the Tax check answer, and one that has not been answered yet carries no route at all. An inner join would drop exactly those cases - the newly imported ones - off the list. {% endcomment %} {% endfetchxml %} {% assign rows = cases.results.entities %} {% assign total = cases.results.total_record_count %}
